verificationCriteria: A page viewed through CMS preview displays content that has been saved but not yet published.
After content is edited and saved without publishing in the CMS, the previewed page displays the edited content.
A page viewed outside of CMS preview displays only published content.
When a previewed page has no saved-but-unpublished version, the page displays the published content.

notes: Novel capability — Live Preview does not exist in this codebase. The Contentstack SDK options object (src/services/contentstack.ts :: options) is the attachment point: live_preview must be enabled there before any downstream query can fetch draft entries. The existing useContent hook and rendering components (ContentstackText, ContentCard, etc.) already consume SDK output and should be reused, not rewritten. Contentstack hosts are unreachable at test time, so VCs are framed at our side of the boundary — what our code requests and renders given a known draft response, and what conditions activate preview mode.

notes: Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria array with helpful context about the attachment point (src/services/contentstack.ts :: options) and the boundary framing. I built all 13 ACs from scratch based on codebase inspection. Key findings from reading the actual files: (1) The `options` object in contentstack.ts has NO `live_preview` property — this is the exact insertion point. (2) `Stack` is created at module level via `contentstack.Stack(options)`, so live preview config must be present at initialization or the Stack must be re-instantiated. (3) No `useContent` hook exists in this codebase — openspec's note about it was inaccurate; data flows through exported functions `getEntry`, `getSingleEntry`, `findSingletonEntry` via `ContentstackFactory`. (4) No existing `live_preview` references anywhere — confirmed this is novel. (5) The existing `isTestEnv()` guard already skips credential validation in test environments, which is relevant for AC-11. AC-9 and AC-12 address the real-time update behavior that distinguishes live preview from a simple draft fetch. AC-5 addresses the story's explicit limitation about protected pages. AC-7/AC-8 ensure the feature is zero-impact when inactive. AC-13 ensures backward compatibility of the existing query API.
